description: Creating a Blog site for "Abandoned but not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars", Creating only frontend of website for NASA Education Blog.
summary:
Abandoned but not Forgotten is an interactive digital storytelling platform built by team CYDROID to uncover the hidden history of humanity's discarded spacecraft, rovers, and scientific instruments on the Moon and Mars.

Designed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, our application transforms static mission archives into an engaging, exploratory experience. Users can [insert core action, e.g., navigate interactive landing sites, inspect 3D models, and read first-person mission logs] to learn how iconic hardware—from Apollo descent stages to retired Martian rovers—contributed to space science before being left behind.

This project matters because space exploration history shouldn't fade into forgotten telemetry logs. By humanizing the machines that paved the way for modern discovery, our platform educates the public, preserves planetary heritage, and sparks vital conversations about sustainable space exploration and off-world artifact preservation.
details:
What It Does & How It Works Abandoned but not Forgotten bridges the gap between raw NASA archival data and accessible public storytelling. Through an intuitive interface, users can explore key landing sites across the Moon and Mars, select individual pieces of discarded equipment, and experience their "life stories"—covering their launch, scientific breakthroughs, final transmissions, and current resting locations.

Intended Impact & Benefits

  • Preserving Space Heritage: Brings attention to historic off-world artifacts that represent humanity's earliest steps beyond Earth.
  • Accessible Education: Turns dense engineering logs and coordinates into compelling narratives for students, educators, and space enthusiasts.
  • Sustainability Awareness: Highlights the growing footprint of human hardware on planetary bodies to inspire responsible future missions.

Tools, Languages & Software Used

  • Frontend / UI: [e.g., React, Next.js, HTML5, CSS3, Tailwind CSS, Three.js]
  • Backend / Data Processing: [e.g., Python, Node.js, JSON]
  • Hosting & Version Control: GitHub ([https://github.com/0x0Abdullah/NASA_App](https://github.com/0x0Abdullah/NASA_App)) and [e.g., Vercel / Netlify / GitHub Pages]

Creativity & Design Considerations Rather than building a dry database, our team focused on emotional resonance and visual clarity. We designed the user journey around storytelling—treating each lander, rover, and discarded stage as a pioneer with a distinct legacy—while grounding every narrative in verified NASA mission records.
